title: Estimates for prior warm, dry summers changed sign between two abundance measures for nine butterflies in Britain in 1980-2024
abstract: We tested whether a warm, dry summer was followed by a lower butterfly abundance index. We used nine species with complete records in England, Scotland and Wales. Separate country models controlled current summer weather and time trends in 1980-2024. A prior summer at +1 C and -100 mm rain gave next-year level estimates of +1.85%, +19.35% and +3.45%. All three country intervals included zero after correction for three tests. The planned annual-change check gave -8.97%, -17.28% and -17.43%. Its corrected intervals also included zero. A direct calculation confirmed that each change estimate equals the level estimate minus the prior-level estimate. Thus a negative annual-change estimate does not alone show a lower next-year level. In separate periods, all level estimates were positive. Only early Scotland had a six-test interval above zero. Its climate contrast required extrapolation. Source models correct gaps in visits and weight sampled flight periods. Checks used site coverage, a fixed species set and records before 2009. This is a small, conditional study. Broad seasonal exposures, few joint warm-dry years, shared regional weather, selected species and unmeasured habitat change limit inference. The data do not show a causal climate effect or establish safety. We did not test air pollution or daily extremes. The package includes exact source snapshots, code, derived evidence, figures and offline checks.

display.caption: Prior summer estimates changed sign between abundance levels and annual changes. Both three-country corrected interval sets included zero. The contrast is +1 C and -100 mm rain relative to 1981-2010.
Primary level estimates in three countries and two periods. Later England and both Scotland period contrasts require extrapolation. Only early Scotland had a six-test period interval above zero.
Nine-species index series and observed prior summer climate. The tested climate point was inside each observed convex hull, but few years exceeded both values.
